headline: Post-Lenalidomide Reset; Earnings Recovery Remains Lumpy

highlights: Business performance: Consolidated revenue fell 29% YoY to Rs9.7bn in Q2FY27.
The decline came mainly from lower lenalidomide revenue, which the growth in the base business including subsidiaries offset partly.
Brazil was the bright spot, with revenue up 66% YoY to Rs1.2bn, and MENA also did well.

EBITDA declined 55.5% YoY to Rs2.6bn, and margin contracted 1,583bps YoY to 26.7% on the lower high-margin lenalidomide contribution and higher R&D spend while reported PAT of Rs2bn includes Rs292mn share from associate Adcock Ingram; additionally Natco raised its stake to 49% during the quarter.
valuation: Outlook: We expect a post-lenalidomide revenue reset, followed by a gradual recovery led by Brazil, India and ROW, with selective upside from US launches.
Valuation: We maintain SELL on Natco Pharma with a revised target price of Rs720 (vs Rs802 earlier), based on 16x Sep’28E EPS of Rs47.

Under its contract it is not targeting RoW semaglutide and is focused on the US and regulated markets.  Ibrutinib litigation is settled and the product was approved within 30 months with exclusivity intact.  Natco has sole FTF on Carfilzomib 10mg, which the management expects to do well.
watch: Outlook: We expect a post-lenalidomide revenue reset, followed by a gradual recovery led by Brazil, India and ROW, with selective upside from US launches.
We treat the Para IV/FTF pipeline as optionality, not assured earnings, given the risk of diluted exclusivity economics.
